To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have overproduced, purified, and crystallized dihydroorotate A, a key enzyme in pyrimidine biosynthesis, and that we have collected X‐ray diffractions data that are of high enough quality to enable us to determine the crystal structure of this enzyme.
the A‐form of the enzyme is a dimeric protein, that it has been crystallized, and that the crystals diffract well.

the A‐form of dihydroorote dehydrogenase has a molecular weight of 68 kDa, is a dimer in solution, is specific for L ‐dihydroorote as substrate, and has a high degree of sequence homology with the B‐form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification and characterization of dihydorotate dehydroganse A from Lactococcus lacticis and with its crystallization.
the purification, characterization, crystallization and X‐ray diffractions studies of dihydroorotase A from L. lactis.
the purification, characterization, and crystallization studies of dihydroorotase A from L. lactis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme is a flavoprotein that catalyzes the oxidation of L‐dihydrorotate to orotate.
this enzyme is the first dihydroorotate reductase that is able to use a respiratory quinone as acceptor.

dihydroorotate A from L. lactis is the first flavoprotein to be crystallized that is capable of using molecular oxygen as electron acceptor, although the enzyme has been crystallised in the absence of molecular oxygen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained crystals suitable for structure determination by X‐ray diffractions.
the dihydroorotate A enzyme from L. lactis is the first enzyme from the pyrimidine de novo synthesis pathway for which crystallographic data are available.
the structure of dihydroorotase A from Lactococcus is being solved at the University of Minnesota, and the structure of dihydororotase B is being solved at EMBL‐Hamburg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dihydroorotate A is a flavoprotein that can use a variety of acceptors for the reducing equivalents, which makes it a potential candidate for a biotechnological application.
the A‐form of dihydroorotase is a flavoprotein, which is a novel feature among dihydroorotases.
the enzyme is very stable and crystallizes well.
